one_month_reasoning: Dycom's own Q3 FY27 report is NOT in the window: the last three Q3 releases came on 2023-11-21, 2024-11-20 and 2025-11-19 (EDGAR [30]), so the likely date is about 2026-11-18 to 11-25, after 2026-11-08. Events inside the window are all indirect. (1) Carrier Q3 results in late October (AT&T, Verizon, etc.) and their capex commentary, the first since the 2026-10-09 SpaceX/Grain 800 MHz spectrum deal knocked carriers down 5.5-7.4% premarket [28]; DY closed down 2.9% that day [7]. Any carrier capex trim is a negative read-across; reassurance is a modest positive. (2) Peer Q3 prints from MasTec, Quanta, MYR Group and Primoris in late October or early November. MasTec cut its Communications guidance by about $400M in Q2 [23], so its comms commentary is the most important read-across. (3) FOMC on Oct 27-28: Kalshi has a 15.5% chance of a hike and 83.5% hold [26]. A surprise hike would hurt this levered, de-rated group. (4) The US midterm elections on Nov 3. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. The stock sits 2% above its 52-week low after a roughly 31% post-earnings slide, and negative momentum and drift argue down. Six weeks have already passed since the print and the shares are at 13x FY28 consensus EPS, so a short-term reversal argues up. I therefore centre slightly below spot (median about $268) with a lognormal sigma of 0.15, which is the given 52% annual vol divided by 3.5.

fair_value.method: A 50/50 blend of two methods: 16x FY28 (Jan-2028) consensus adjusted EPS of $20.78 gives $332, and 10x an estimated FY28 EBITDA of $1.244B, less about $2.30B of net debt over 30.36M diluted shares, gives $334. Both multiples sit inside the bottom half of the 12-peer range, discounted for leverage, the adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap and customer concentration.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus $20.78 (+21.9% y/y). Alpha Vantage average of $20.78 from 5 analysts, up from $19.95 30 days earlier, so estimates were not cut after Q2.

The 12-peer forward P/E median is 23.3x (range 15.2-38.3x). DY traded at 22.4x pre-Q2 while MTZ was at 25.1x and MYRG at 25.6x, about 11% below its closest telecom peers [29]. I apply about a 30% discount to the peer median, which puts 16x between LMB/GVA (15.2-15.8x) and MTZ (19.9x). Reasons: adjusted EPS excludes amortization, and Q2 GAAP diluted EPS was $3.81 against $5.29 adjusted (28% lower) [1]. Net debt is about $2.5B versus net cash at most peers [2][4]. The 2026 macro is a hiking cycle [26]. 16x is above today's 13.0x because the FY28 estimates have held up.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue $8.58B x 14.5% EBITDA margin = $1.244B; x 10.0x = EV $12.44B; minus net debt ~$2.30B = $10.14B equity / 30.36M diluted shares = $334

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis: $8.58B (+13.2%). Alpha Vantage average: $8.583B from 6 analysts.

FY27 margins: Q1 13.4% ($262.5M/$1,965M), Q2 15.7% ($315.5M/$2,005.9M), Q3 guide midpoint 15.0% ($291.5M/$1,940M), a 14.7% blend. Q4 is seasonally weaker. Management expects the consolidated margin to rise y/y, with Communications slightly down and Building Systems in the high teens to low twenties. 14.5% is roughly flat on the FY27 run-rate.

Peer TTM EV/EBITDA median 17.3x (range 11.0-36.9x). Peers' forward P/E averages about 0.77x their trailing P/E (median trailing/forward ratio 1.31), which implies a peer forward EV/EBITDA near 13x. DY today trades at 11.6x TTM [4] and about 8.7x FY28 EBITDA. I use 10x, roughly 23% below the implied peer forward median, for the same leverage and concentration reasons as the P/E method.

Q2 FY27 notional net debt was $2,502.6M [2], and StockAnalysis shows net debt of $2.70B [4]. I deduct about $200M for H2 seasonal free cash flow (Q2 FCF was $37.9M with H1 at -$54.2M) to Oct-2027. This is a judgment; management gives no FCF guide.
Q2 FY27 weighted-average diluted shares were 30,363,819. StockAnalysis shows 30.16M outstanding.

bear.story: The 2018 analog repeats. Carrier capex is trimmed after the SpaceX spectrum shock, wireless deferrals spread, fuel costs and the hiking cycle squeeze margins, and FY28 EPS is cut to about $16 (-23% vs consensus). The stock de-rates to about 11x, which gives about $180. In 2018 DY fell 36-52% within a year of its guidance warning.

base.story: Backlog of $12.2B (+53%) converts and the deferred $150M wireless revenue lands in FY28. FY28 EPS comes in near $20 and the multiple partly recovers to about 15x. The group de-rating persists while the Fed is hiking, so the stock stays below fair value.

bull.story: Estimates hold or rise ($21.5+), the Fed pauses, and BEAD construction and hyperscaler fiber visibly ramp. DY re-rates to about 20.5x, still below the peer median, giving about $440. That is a partial retrace toward the pre-Q2 level of about $390-420.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 15.2x (GVA) to 38.3x (PWR). EV/EBITDA, TTM because no forward figure is published on the source, 11.0x (LMB) to 36.9x (PWR).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DY spot is 13.0x FY28 EPS and 14.6x forward P/E on the source, below the bottom of the peer range. EV/EBITDA is 11.6x TTM, bottom quartile. We use 16x P/E and 10x forward EV/EBITDA, both inside the range but in its lower part and about 30% below the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount reflects structural factors that will persist through Oct-2027. (1) Leverage: notional net debt is $2.50B, about 2.7-2.9x TTM EBITDA, after the Power Solutions purchase [2][4]. Most peers (EME, FIX, STRL, IESC, AGX, MYRG) have EV at or below market cap, i.e. net cash. (2) Earnings quality: adjusted EPS excludes acquisition amortization, and Q2 GAAP EPS of $3.81 was 28% below the $5.29 adjusted figure [1]. Peers' forward P/Es are on less adjusted bases. (3) Customer concentration in a few telecom carriers whose economics were just challenged by SpaceX's spectrum push [28], with wireless deferrals already hitting DY and MTZ [1][23]. (4) History: even before the selloff DY traded about 11% below MTZ and MYRG on forward P/E [29]. We do NOT use sell-side 'outperform' calls or the $521 mean target.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is about 9.6x FY28 consensus EPS and roughly 8x EBITDA after net debt. At that level the market would be pricing a 2018-style earnings reset (in 2018 full-year EPS guidance was cut about 44% [20]) rather than the de-rating seen so far, in which estimates have actually risen. It is also 24% below the 52-week low of $263, beyond a one-sigma annual move from a level that already embeds the post-Q2 de-rating. Trading there would most likely mean a carrier or hyperscaler program cut, a guidance reset, or a balance-sheet or covenant problem.

catalysts.event: AT&T/Verizon/Lumen/Comcast Q3 results and capex commentary, the first since the SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal
MasTec, Quanta, MYR Group and Primoris Q3 results; read-across on communications and data-center demand
US midterm elections (policy on broadband, tariffs and energy)
DY Q3 FY27 results vs guide (rev $1.90-1.98B, adj EPS $4.33-4.79); first comments on FY28
FOMC (Kalshi 71.5% / Polymarket 74.5% hike odds); a hike pressures levered, de-rated contractors
Q4 FY27 results and first formal FY28 outlook (consensus EPS $20.78)
BEAD-funded construction ramps after all 56 final proposals were approved on 2026-08-25
Q1/Q2 FY28 results: whether the ~$150M deferred wireless revenue and the $12.2B backlog convert
FCC/regulatory approval of SpaceX spectrum acquisitions; carrier competitive response

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 de-rating of telecom/utility contractors (DY -52%, MTZ and PRIM down 45-59% from highs) is a macro/rates event or the start of an earnings-cycle downturn like DY in 2018-19.
Carrier capex after SpaceX's spectrum push. DY's largest customers are telecom carriers, and wireless work has already been deferred ($150M into FY28).
The Fed hiking path: Kalshi puts December hike odds at about 72%. Elevated oil and fuel costs hit Communications margins directly.
Leverage of about $2.5B in net debt and the quality of adjusted EPS (28% above GAAP in Q2).
Timing of BEAD construction and hyperscaler long-haul fiber programs versus backlog conversion.

Base-rate evidence is mixed. DY's own history after 45%+ drawdowns is poor: across all days in drawdown the median 12-month return was -13% with 44% positive, and the 2018 warning led to -36% to -47%. Peer episodes are far better: median about +36%, 15 of 19 positive, but with survivorship bias.
reasoning: Facts: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 45.6% (16.7% organic), adjusted EPS was $5.29, backlog was $12.24B (+53%), and FY27 revenue guidance went to $7.48-7.66B. About $150M of wireless revenue was deferred into FY28 and Communications margins slipped [1][2]. The stock fell 21.6% in the week after the print [21] and has kept falling to $269. Consensus FY27/FY28 EPS of $17.05/$20.78 has actually risen over the last 30 days [5][6], so this is a multiple de-rating from about 22x forward pre-Q2 [29] to 13x FY28, not an earnings collapse. Macro backdrop: Kalshi and Polymarket price about 72% odds of a December Fed hike [26] after 2026's oil and inflation shock [24], 2027 recession odds are 20% [25], and SpaceX's spectrum deal hit DY's carrier customers on Oct 9 [28]. Base rates (computed from Twelve Data histories [7]): unconditional DY 12-month forward return median +23% with 68% positive over 2007-2026 (a strong secular uptrend). Conditional on being 45%+ below the 52-week high, DY's own days show median -13% with 44% positive, dominated by 2008 and 2018-19. Event analog: after the Aug-2018 guidance warning (FY EPS cut ~44% [20]) DY fell another 36-47% over 12 months. After the Aug-2025 Q2 miss (-11%) DY rose +45-53% over 12 months. Pooled peer drawdown episodes (MTZ, PRIM, MYRG, PWR, EME, FIX): median about +36%, 15 of 19 positive, but survivorship-biased. I weight DY's mixed own history against the more favourable peer and estimate-revision evidence and land at P(up) of about 56-57%. Valuation: a 16x P/E and 10x EV/EBITDA blend gives $333 fair value, inside the peer range but discounted for leverage, the GAAP gap and concentration. I do not expect full convergence while the Fed hikes, so the 12-month median is about $290 (+8%). The distribution is lognormal-like with sigma about 0.45 (given realized vol 52%, slightly lower forward) and a fattened left tail for the 2018-type and leverage risk. Scenario mean is about $308 (25% at $180 / 50% at $305 / 25% at $440). Sell-side targets (mean $521 [5]) were not used as an anchor. Research limits: Zacks and macrotrends pages were bot-blocked or 403 and were not worked around. Peer forward EV/EBITDA was not available, so TTM is shown. Twelve Data statistics and earnings endpoints were plan-restricted.
